_about: Generated from annotations.json by remapping addresses through

headers.f6:4000:
----------------------------------------------------------------
BANK 6 ENTRY VECTOR TABLE
Bank 6 is permanently mapped at $4000-$7FFF (a78 cart type bit 4),
so these five slots are the only stable entry points into the engine.
Code running out of the paged $8000-$BFFF window calls them by address.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:400F:
DLI (display list interrupt) handler.
MARIA raises NMI at the end of a zone whose DL header has the DLI bit
set.  $400C jumps through the RAM vector at $2135/$2136 so the engine
can chain a different handler per zone.
headers.f7:FEB5:
----------------------------------------------------------------
PER-AREA DESCRIPTOR TABLES  (9 entries, index 0 unused)
  $FEB5 tbl_AreaPage   -> high byte ($80/$A0) of the area's data in the
                          $8000-$BFFF window; stored over area_page
  $FEBE tbl_AreaBank   -> ROM bank to page into $8000 for this area
  $FEC7/$FED0 tbl_AreaPtrLo/Hi -> pointer into $DA00-$DCFF (bank 7)
  $FED9 tbl_AreaType   -> area/level type code
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:404A:
dli_index has run past the last zone: end of the visible
field.  Re-arm the vector for the next frame, page in bank 0 for
the per-frame work, then restore the game's bank.
headers.b0:A22F:
----------------------------------------------------------------
TEXT RENDERER
Walks a string record and blits one glyph per character.
  $A2AC  classify: C=1 for space/'|'/'*'/'&'/$80+ (a break), C=0 for a glyph
  $A2C6  newline: destination pointer += $16 (22 columns per row)
  $A2C2  new page: reset column then newline
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:4D1E:
Startup palette: 24 bytes copied to MARIA $28-$3F at $4A68,
skipping every 4th register (those are MSTAT/DPPH/DPPL/CHARBASE/
OFFSET/CTRL, not colours).  So this fills P2C1..P7C3.
headers.b0:A32B:
----------------------------------------------------------------
GrampaPickMessage -- returns X = message number for the table at
tbl_MsgPtrLo/Hi.  First match wins:
    forced_msg  != 0 -> (forced_msg & $7F) | $20
    undead_flag != 0 -> $0C  "YOU'RE ONE OF THE UNDEAD"
    win_flag     > 0 -> $0D  "OH WHAT A RELIEF! YOU SAVED ME!"
    death_state != 0 and revive_ok == 0 -> $0B  "HIT RESET TO RESTART"
    death_state != 0 and revive_ok != 0 -> $0F  resurrection (below)
    otherwise -> the hint pool
Confirmed by replaying a recorded session in MAME:
  hp_max $4F, died -> revive_ok latched -> revived with hp_max $27,
  which is exactly ((old >> 1) & $F8) | $07.
  Died again at hp_max $27 (below the $30 threshold): revive_ok never
  latched, no resurrection, the run ended.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b0:A608:
Message pointer table, 50 entries, low bytes then high bytes.
Each pointer aims at the record's two header bytes: p1 -> txt_pal,
p2 -> index into the indent table at $A4B2.  The text itself starts
at the following '@'.  Slot $0E duplicates $0F and is never loaded.
headers.b0:A05C:
Sound-effect sequence pointers, indexed by sfx_request*2.
A sequence is a byte stream read by SfxUpdate: values < $10 go to
AUDC0, values >= $10 go to AUDF0 with the high nibble as AUDV0,
and $00 ends the sequence.
headers.f6:4E73:
CheckDeathCondition -- sets death_state to $FF when either
hp_cur or blood_purity reaches 0, and switches area_type to $0A
(the death scene).
headers.f6:4E91:
StatusTick -- runs every 8th frame (frame_ctr & 7 == 0).
While alive it latches revive_ok = $FF when blood_purity != 0,
hp_max >= $30 and mode_flag == 0.  If blood_purity has hit 0 it
sets undead_flag instead, which is why a blood death can never be
resurrected -- "I CAN'T PURIFY YOUR BLOOD".
headers.f6:51EC:
CollectItem -- item_type indexes the inventory counters at
$1F3D.  Item $08 (diamond) raises hp_max by 8 and refills hp_cur.
Item $06 (potion) restores 50 blood_purity, capped at 100, but
only once two have been collected.
headers.b0:BDC2:
DbgPauseHook -- reached from $A31F only while the console
PAUSE switch is held (SWCHB bit 3 clear).  Steps dbg_step on a
button press and, once past 3, grants +8 hp_max and full
blood_purity.  Left-over debug code: the intermediate states branch
to $BE0E/$BE13, which are inside the sound data below, so the
bonus cannot actually be reached without crashing first.
headers.f6:506F:
----------------------------------------------------------------
UseSelectedItem -- sel_item ($CC) is the slot chosen on the Grampa
menu.  Only the two potions do anything here:
    $06 red potion   blood_purity += 50, capped at 100
    $07 blue potion  hp_cur = hp_max, and the item is consumed
Item numbers index the inventory counters at $1F3D (16 slots,
slot 0 unused) and the icon tables at $5195/$51A5.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5779:
----------------------------------------------------------------
TerrainDispatch -- A holds the terrain/object code under Jimmy.
    $A0        healing well: +1 hp_cur per tick (see below)
    $8C/$8E/$8F  other terrain handlers
    $EF        destroyed with sel_item $05 -> sets win_flag
    >= $F0     handled by $5810
Returns carry set when the terrain consumed the step.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:57AA:
Terrain_HealingWell -- the well.  Adds a single point of health
per call, clamped to hp_max, and re-triggers sound $0A.  It never
touches hp_max, which is why standing at the well refills the bar
but does not extend it -- only diamonds do that.
headers.f7:D243:
----------------------------------------------------------------
MapTileAt -- look up the terrain under a world position.
  in:  Y = cross-axis position, X = long-axis low, A = long-axis high
  out: A = terrain code (0 when out of bounds)

    strip   = tbl_MapStrip[Y >> 4]     ten 100-byte bands
    cell    = strip[longaxis >> 3]
    terrain = area_ptr[cell >> 1]

The ten bands live at $2400, $2464 ... $2784.  Confirmed in MAME:
those same addresses are the data pointers of the live display list
at $2200, whose 5-byte MARIA headers have the indirect bit set --

    00 60 24 2B 00   -> data $2400, indirect, palette 1, width 21
    64 60 24 0B 00   -> data $2464, indirect, palette 0, width 21

so MARIA reads this memory as a character map while the CPU reads it
as terrain.  One byte per cell does both jobs: the byte is the
character number MARIA draws, and byte >> 1 indexes the per-area
terrain table.  That is why the cartridge holds no separate map.

Observed live grid bytes are all even and all below $80, exactly the
doubled indices this routine expects.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:55E6:
CheckTerrainUnderPlayer -- converts the player position
(player_x + $0C, player_y - $18) into world coordinates and calls
MapTileAt.  Terrain 0 is empty; anything with bit 7 set is latched
into pending_terrain for HandlePendingTerrain to act on.
headers.f6:5681:
HandlePendingTerrain -- runs the terrain code latched in
pending_terrain by CheckTerrainUnderPlayer.  Codes $81-$8F trigger
scripted events; $A0 is the healing well; $EF is the final target;
$F0 and above are handled at $5810.
headers.b3:8000:
----------------------------------------------------------------
BuildArea -- unpacks the current area.  Called once with bank 3
paged in ($4A9D-$4AA4).

Walks a record stream through src_ptr, five bytes per record:
    $80        the next two bytes are a new src_ptr (follow it)
    $FE        clear the $93 flag
    $FF        end of stream
    otherwise  the lead byte is the row the record belongs to; it is
               compared with build_row and the record skipped unless
               they match.  The remaining four bytes are a MARIA
               4-byte display list header, copied to build_dst.

build_pass ($90) selects which of two parallel display structures is
being built:
    pass 0 -> list data at $2200, pointers into the DLL-format table
              at $1800
    pass 1 -> list data at $2400, pointers into the table at $1B00
tbl_RowDLLOffset ($8222) gives each row's offset into those tables,
in steps of 3 -- MARIA display list list entry size.

The $2400 buffer's character maps are also the terrain grid that
MapTileAt reads -- the display list points at them in indirect mode,
so one set of bytes is both what MARIA draws and what the player
collides with.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:73FA:
----------------------------------------------------------------
CREDITS -- shown on the run of screens before the final boss.
Second text framing: <$FE|$FF> <p1> <p2> then the text, running to
the next $FE/$FF.  No '@' introducer and no '#' terminator, unlike
the Grampa message records in bank 0.
  PRODUCED BY RADIOACTIVE SOFTWARE
  COPYRIGHT 1990 ATARI CORP, ALL RIGHTS RESERVED
  PROGRAM AND DESIGN BY PETER ADAMS
  STORIES BY TAMMY MOORE
  MUSIC AND SOUND BY PAUL WEBB
  SPECIAL THANKS TO ADAM CLAYTON AND RICH ROBBINS
  ART BY LES PARDUE
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b3:8124:
----------------------------------------------------------------
BuildWalkStream -- the area record stream, five bytes per record:

    <row> <gfx_lo> <pal|width> <gfx_hi> <hpos>

The lead byte is the row the record belongs to; it is compared with
build_row ($46) and the record is skipped unless they match.  The
remaining four bytes are copied verbatim to build_dst and are a
standard MARIA 4-byte display list header:
    gfx_lo/gfx_hi  graphics address
    pal|width      palette in bits 7-5, width in bits 4-0 as a
                   5-bit two's complement count
    hpos           horizontal position

Lead bytes $80, $FE and $FF are escapes rather than rows: $80 means
the next two bytes are a new src_ptr to follow, $FE clears the $93
flag, $FF ends the stream.

Example, from the stream at $8377:
    08 1A 7A B0 55  -> row 8, gfx $B01A, palette 3, width 6, x $55
    0A 5C 7C B0 5D  -> row 10, gfx $B05C, palette 3, width 4, x $5D
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b3:829C: Per-screen stream pointers, indexed by screen_idx*2.
headers.b0:BDE6:
DbgReadButtons -- the only safe path through DbgPauseHook.
Requires INPT1 held (bit 7 set = pressed) and INPT0, INPT2 and INPT3
all released; anything else branches to $BE0E or $BE13, which are
inside the sound data and reach a BRK within a few bytes.  The IRQ
vector is $FF00, the reset entry, so a wrong button resets the
console rather than hanging.
headers.f7:DA00:
----------------------------------------------------------------
PER-AREA TERRAIN PROPERTY TABLES -- six tables of 128 entries.
area_ptr ($C0/$C1) selects one; MapTileAt indexes it with the grid
cell byte shifted right one place, so a cell selects one of these
entries and the entry is the terrain code.

Low codes are collision classes in bits 0-1 (see $561C):
    0  open
    1  blocks in the lower-right half of the cell
    2  blocks in the upper-left half of the cell
    3  solid
Classes 1 and 2 are the two halves of a diagonal, which is how the
angled paths and walls are built.  Bits 2 and above are further
flags carried in terrain_byte; values $05, $06, $07 and $0B occur.

Codes with bit 7 set are events, latched into pending_terrain:
$81-$8F scripted triggers, $A0 the healing well, $A1, $EF the final
target, and $F1-$F3.  $DA80 -- shared by areas 2, 5 and 6 -- is the
one holding both $A0 entries and the single $EF.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:561D:
Collision test.  cell_half ($50) is 1 or 2 depending on which
side of the cell diagonal the player stands: sub_x + 2*sub_y < $10
puts them in the upper-left half.  A terrain class equal to
cell_half blocks, as does class 3; class 0 never blocks.
noclip ($1FDD) suppresses blocking entirely.
headers.b3:80E6:
Store this row's list pointer into the DLL-format table for the
current pass: $1800 for pass 0, $1B00 for pass 1.  Entries are three
bytes, so the offsets in tbl_RowDLLOffset step by 3.
headers.f7:D800:
Display list list for the message/Grampa screen, copied to $2600.
3 bytes per zone. Zones 6-21 are 16 message rows of 8 scanlines; each
row's list is at $2663 + row*15 and reads the character map at
$2400 + row*22, giving 16 rows of 22 characters. Two overlaid 16-byte
art runs at x $00 draw the portrait from b0:$9000-$9FFF in palettes 7
and 1.
headers.b3:8276:
----------------------------------------------------------------
FlipDisplayBuffer -- the game is double buffered.

Waits on MSTAT for the end of the visible field, then points MARIA at
whichever buffer was just finished and switches build_pass so the
next BuildArea pass fills the other one:

    buffer A   DLL at $1800   display lists from $2200
    buffer B   DLL at $1B00   display lists from $2400

InitBothDLLs ($8265) seeds both DLLs from tbl_DLLTemplate, 58 bytes
= 19 three-byte entries.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:4D42:
tick_slow ($47) round-robins the heavy subsystems: its low two
bits select which of four update routines runs this pass, so each
runs once every four ticks.  Other readers use it for animation
phase ($6040) and to halve its rate again ($5AEF).  Measured in MAME
it advances about once every 240 frames.
headers.f6:7690:
Start song A: copy the two voice track pointers out of SongTable,
build the voice-enable mask, prime both voices.
headers.b3:85FC:
----------------------------------------------------------------
FadeToBlack -- ramp every zone palette down to colour $00.

Walks MARIA's colour registers (skipping every fourth, which are
control registers), subtracts from the luma nibble of each entry,
and writes both zone_pal_shadow and the live register.  $41 counts
how many entries still changed; the routine repeats, with a delay
loop at $8633, until everything reads zero.

DARKNESS, measured across three recorded playthroughs:
counting non-zero bytes in the 44-byte zone palette block,
    lit outdoor area          34 of 44
    cave without the lantern   4 of 44   (zone 10 only -- the status
                                          bar; zones 0-9 all $00)
    cave carrying the lantern 34 of 44
The lantern is inventory item $09.  A run that entered the cave with
it and with boss_flags still $00 lit normally, so the gate is the
item and not boss progress.

There is no separate dark render path: the character map, display
lists and collision keep running, so the player moves and enemies
still kill them.  Every play-area colour is simply black.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b5:B637:
BossSequenceReward -- confirmed in MAME.  mode_flag went 0 -> 2 on
entering the boss fight and 2 -> 0 on completion, and on that exact
frame hp_max rose $37 -> $47, the +$10 this routine applies, with
blood_purity restored to $64.
headers.b5:B651:
On completing a boss the sequence ORs that boss's bit from
tbl_BossBit into boss_flags ($1FBC), then clears mode_flag to hand
control back.  boss_flags is the game's progression bitfield: it is
cleared at startup ($4ABC) and only ever gains bits here.
headers.f6:56E1:
----------------------------------------------------------------
Terrain events gated on boss progress.

  terrain $85: with sel_item $02 -> forced_msg $81 (story $21)
               otherwise requires boss_flags bit 0; if clear, just
               draws glyph $38 and refuses
  terrain $86: requires boss_flags bit 0; if clear, draws glyph $39
               and refuses.  When open -> forced_msg $82 (story $22)

forced_msg feeds GrampaPickMessage, which turns it into message
index (forced_msg & $7F) | $20 -- so these are the story screens.

This is the ordering mechanism: a boss must be beaten before these
terrain squares will do anything.  Reported from play: entering the
mansion basement the back way skipped the trigger and the blaster
would not spawn; re-entering through the gated square fired story
$22 and the sequence then ran normally.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5859:
----------------------------------------------------------------
CheckGhostTouch -- the only thing in the game that reduces hp_max.

Two dedicated actor slots, each with its own position pair and an
active flag tested through bit 7.  If either is active and the
collision test at $5A2F reports a hit, DrainMaxHealth runs:

    terrain_timer = $28        40-frame cooldown, so it drains at
                               most once every 40 frames of contact
    if hp_max < $11: do nothing        floor of 17 -- the drain can
                                       never take you below it
    blank one health-bar cell at $23E7 + (hp_max >> 3)
    hp_max -= 8
    if hp_cur > hp_max: hp_cur = hp_max

Two slots rather than the general enemy array, which fits these
being the ghosts: the in-game hint at $BA6D warns that they drain
life, and they appear in only a couple of places.  Every other
source moves hp_max upward (diamonds +8, boss reward +$10); this is
the sole counterweight.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f7:F00C:
----------------------------------------------------------------
LoadAreaHeader -- reads the area's header fields from the stream at
src_ptr: page, the darkness flag, map limits and the first object.

  $F01C  area_is_dark ($1EC5) <- the area's darkness byte
  $F021  if cnt_lantern ($1F46) is non-zero, force area_is_dark = 0

That is the whole lantern check.  Carrying item $09 clears the
area's darkness flag as the area loads; nothing else is involved.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f7:F12B:
----------------------------------------------------------------
InstallAreaPalette -- copies 40 palette bytes from the area
descriptor into pal_target ($1EF8), which the ramp then walks the
live shadow ($1ECC) toward.

If area_is_dark is set, every byte is passed through
    AND #$08 : LSR : LSR
so a colour becomes $02 when bit 3 was set and $00 otherwise -- black
or near-black across the whole play area.  The status bar sits in
zone 10 and is written elsewhere, which is why it stays readable
while the game area is invisible.

Measured across recorded runs: 34 of 44 palette bytes non-zero in a
lit area, 4 of 44 in the cave without the lantern, 34 of 44 with it.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6043:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ActorMoveAndAnimate -- per-actor motion, animation and despawn.
X is the actor slot.

Actors live in six parallel zero-page arrays of 8 entries each,
stride 8, so eight slots:
    $8F  position, long axis      $9F  velocity, long axis
    $97  position, cross axis     $A7  velocity, cross axis
    $AF  active flag              $B7  (not yet identified)

actor_slot_to_disp ($1FDE,X) maps a slot to its display index Y,
which selects into a second set of arrays the display builder reads:
    $1DF8 active   $1E08 pos long   $1E18 pos cross   $1E28 graphic

Each call:
  - animation frame = tbl at $6081 indexed by tick_slow & 3, giving
    the four-frame cycle $80/$82/$84/$86
  - position += world_drift ($8E) + this actor's velocity, so the
    scroll is folded into actor motion rather than applied separately
  - despawn (clear actor_active and disp_active) once the position
    passes $C0 or the derived screen row leaves the visible range

This is the movement substrate.  What chooses each actor's velocity
-- the actual behaviour -- has not been traced yet.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5F8D:
----------------------------------------------------------------
Contact damage from actor X -- blood purity, not health.

A bounding-box overlap test against the player (+/-$1C long axis,
+/-$0C cross axis), then:

    if sel_item == $01        -> no loss at all
    otherwise                 -> DrainBloodPurity once
    if cnt_cross ($1F3E) == 0 -> DrainBloodPurity a second time

Item $01 has two tiers: SELECTED blocks the hit outright, merely
OWNED halves the loss.  That is the cross, and it explains why bats,
crows and crabs -- the blood drainers -- are harmless while it is
held.  Item $04 (the Heart) blocks the loss further down, inside
DrainBloodPurity itself.

A $14 cooldown in terrain_timer rate-limits repeat contact.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f7:D423:
----------------------------------------------------------------
DrainBloodPurity -- reached through the bank 7 vector $D039.
Costs one point of blood_purity, with two ways out:

    death_state != 0   -> nothing (already dying)
    cnt_heart ($1F41)  -> nothing at all; item $04 grants outright
                          immunity to blood loss, which matches the
                          Heart's described role of permanently
                          purifying the blood
    blood_purity == 0  -> nothing (already at zero)

This is the ONLY thing this primitive does, so every caller of $D039
is a blood-purity source, not a health source.  Health damage runs
through a different path.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5BCF:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ActorDispatch -- runs all 8 slots.  actor_mode ($AF,X) is a mode
field, NOT a hit-point count:

    $00        empty slot
    $01-$7F    death animation countdown.  The value indexes
               tbl_DeathFrames for this frame's graphic, then is
               decremented; on reaching 0 the actor is removed from
               the display.
    $80-$FF    live actor; the value selects its behaviour --
               $FF -> $5C13,  $FE -> $5DBD,  $FD -> ActorMoveAndAnimate

So there is no health value anywhere in the actor structure.  An
enemy is "killed" by writing a small positive number into
actor_mode, which flips it out of its behaviour and into an N-frame
death animation.  Nothing subtracts damage, so every kill is a one
hit kill by construction -- which matches play: the knife despatches
crows, bats and wolves instantly, while enemies it cannot kill only
flash and keep going, because their behaviour was never replaced.

Leaving the play area is a separate path: ActorMoveAndAnimate clears
actor_mode and disp_active directly at $607B, bypassing the death
animation entirely.  An enemy that wanders off screen is gone
without ever having been killed.
Replaying axe and blaster sessions showed kills arriving as a
single write of $08 into actor_mode from $FF, with no counter moving
in the $80/$83 arrays for that slot.  That is NOT sufficient to
conclude there are no hit points: play reports 20-30 hits to kill
these zombies, and only two kills were detected in a three-minute
axe run, so the sampled slot and window may simply not cover the
engagement being described.  A hit counter dedicated to the zombie
type remains the most likely explanation and has not been ruled out.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b0:A4D4:
----------------------------------------------------------------
DrawInventoryMenu -- the Grampa item screen.

The weapon is drawn FIRST and separately, from weapon_level ($86)
indexed into dat0_A552; a negative value means no weapon yet.  The
weapon is a single upgrading slot, not an inventory entry:
    none -> knife -> axe -> blaster -> mega blaster

Then a loop walks inventory slots 7 down to 1 -- LDX #$07 with BNE,
so slot 0 and everything from $08 up are never displayed.  The
cursor wraps with AND #$07 at $A537, confirming eight positions.

Confirmed against play, the seven selectable slots are:
    $01 cross            $05 plasmic pumpkin
    $02 crypt key        $06 purity potion (red)
    $03 necklace         $07 health potion (blue)
    $04 heart

Each agrees with a separately derived mechanism: $01 blocks contact
blood loss, $04 makes DrainBloodPurity a no-op, $05 is the item
tested against terrain $EF that sets win_flag, $02 is tested against
terrain $85, and $06/$07 are the two potions in UseSelectedItem.

Counters at $08 and above are not menu items -- diamonds, the
lantern and other tallies live there.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:50C7:
----------------------------------------------------------------
Applies a weapon's properties after weapon_level ($86) changes.
Clears sel_item, then sets weapon_cooldown ($88) from the table at
$50ED indexed by level:

    0 knife $28   1 axe $1E   2 blaster $14   3 mega blaster $0A

Lower is faster, so the weapon progression is partly a fire-rate
upgrade.  Level 2 additionally sets $1E72.

The pickup path reaches this from $5208: item_type $0C-$0F becomes
weapon_level via SBC #$0C, so $0C knife, $0D axe, $0E blaster,
$0F mega blaster.  Those are pickup type codes, a different
namespace from the seven inventory menu slots.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:4FE5:
----------------------------------------------------------------
FireWeapon -- the attack, driven by the debounced fire button
($1FC0).  Bails out if dead, if an item is selected (that path runs
UseSelectedItem instead), if weapon_level is negative (no weapon),
or if fire_timer ($87) is still counting.

Projectiles live in THREE slots, indexed by X = 2..0, in their own
parallel arrays -- a separate structure from the 8-slot actor arrays:
    $74 position long    $7A type      $83 graphic
    $77 position cross   $7D unknown   $80 unknown

A free slot is one whose proj_type has bit 7 set.  On firing:

    proj_type  = weapon_level * 4 + direction
    proj_gfx   = tbl_ProjGfx[proj_type]
    position   = player position + per-weapon offset from
                 tbl_ProjSpawnLong / tbl_ProjSpawnCross
    fire_timer = weapon_cooldown        <- the rate limit
    sfx        = weapon_level + 1

So every attack spawns a projectile carrying the weapon's own icon,
and weapon_level reaches the enemy only through that projectile.

NOTE: $80 and $83 belong to this projectile structure, NOT to the
actor arrays.  An earlier search for enemy hit points read them as
if they were 8-slot actor fields, which they are not; that search
was invalid and proved nothing.

DIRECTION LOCK DURING BOSS FIGHTS ($5015):

    LDY mode_flag
    BEQ normal                  ; ordinary play: direction comes from
                                ; the player's facing, via $54BB
    LDA weapon_level
    ASL A : ASL A
    ADC boss_fire_dir ($1EA9)   ; boss fight: direction is FIXED, from
  normal:                       ; a per-boss constant set in bank 5
    STA proj_type,X

So in a boss fight the player does not aim.  proj_type is built from
weapon_level * 4 plus a constant the boss sequence writes to
boss_fire_dir at b5:$B076, which is why each boss pins the player to
one firing direction -- upward for some, left for another -- and why
the boss's own projectiles travel along the matching axis.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5D5F:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ProjectileVsActors -- every projectile against every actor, and the
place a kill is decided.  On a bounding-box overlap:

    JSR sub_4F6C            despawn the projectile
    LDA actor_mode,X
    CMP #$A0
    BCS kill                already at or past $A0 -> dies now
    ADC weapon_level        <-- THE DAMAGE MODEL
    STA actor_mode,X
    CMP #$A0
    BCS kill                crossed $A0 -> dies
    sfx $13, actor_flash_timer = $1E     hit, but still alive
  kill:
    actor_mode = $08        death countdown, sfx $12

actor_mode is BOTH the behaviour selector and the toughness counter.
A hit adds weapon_level to it and death is reaching $A0.  So:

    knife  level 0  adds NOTHING -- can never kill anything that
                    starts below $A0, however long you hit it
    axe    level 1  +1 per hit
    blaster        +2 per hit
    mega blaster   +3 per hit

Enemies already at $A0 or above -- crows, bats, wolves at mode $FE
or $FF -- skip the addition entirely and die to any hit, including
the knife's zero-damage one.  An enemy starting at $80 needs $20 (32)
points: 32 axe hits, 16 blaster hits, and never with the knife.

The flash on a non-fatal hit is actor_flash_timer, $1E frames.  That
is why an enemy the knife cannot kill still flickers on every hit --
the hit registers, the flash fires, and the counter gains zero.

SPAWN VALUES, and therefore enemy toughness.  Toughness is simply
$A0 minus the value an actor is spawned with, so the spawn constant
IS the enemy's health:

    $5C77  mode $FF   already past $A0 -> dies to any hit
    $5E37  mode $FE   likewise
    $60C6  mode $FD   likewise, uses ActorMoveAndAnimate
    $5ED6  mode $98   needs 8 points: 8 axe hits, 4 blaster hits,
                      never with the knife

So "tougher" enemies are literally spawned with a lower number.  The
three high values are the one-hit kills (crows, bats, wolves); $98 is
the first genuinely tough spawn found.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6088:
----------------------------------------------------------------
TryThrowProjectile -- in: X = thrower position long, Y = cross.

Throws only when the player is OUTSIDE a box around the thrower:
    |dx| >= $40 (measured via +$20 / CMP #$40), or
    |dy| >= $30 (via +$18 / CMP #$30)
Inside that box it returns without throwing, so a projectile enemy
stops shooting once you close the distance.

Otherwise it falls into SpawnEnemyProjectile, which takes the first
free slot of the eight-slot actor array, seeds position from the
thrower, computes a velocity via $5CEE, and sets actor_mode to $FD
-- the straight-line ActorMoveAndAnimate behaviour.

$FD is above $A0, so any player shot destroys a projectile in one
hit.  That is why player and enemy projectiles annihilate: it needs
no special case, just the ordinary damage model.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6328:
The throw is gated by throw_enable ($1FCC) and a rate mask
($8D); the thrower's position comes from sactor_pos_long ($DD,X)
and sactor_pos_cross ($E1,X).

Those arrays are the SPECIAL ACTOR structure -- enemies that are not
in the eight-slot actor array.  The projectile-throwing cave zombies
live here, as do the pumpkin-headed throwers, alongside sactor_facing
($1E8D,X).  This is the system that also holds the ghosts, and it is
why searching the eight-slot arrays never found the tough enemies.
headers.f7:F057:
----------------------------------------------------------------
Area header, continued -- this is where region-specific content is
defined.  Every field comes from the area's own record stream, so
each area gets its own cast:

  item_type ($1E80)   the item that appears in this area
  $EF special case    if the byte is $EF the value becomes $22 when
                      the player already holds the cross, else $FF
  six values expanded through $F280 into pairs:
      $1E6A/$1E6B  $1E6C/$1E6D  $1E6E/$1E6F
      $1E70/$1E71  $1E72/$1E73  $1E74/$1E75
                      the per-area SPECIAL ACTOR definitions -- the
                      four-slot cast that holds ghosts, the throwing
                      cave zombies and the pumpkin-headed throwers
  throw_enable ($1FCC) whether this area's enemies throw projectiles
                      at all; TryThrowProjectile checks it first
  $1E76, $1E77, $1E7D, $1E7E  further per-area fields

So "only spawns in the caves" is not spawn logic at all: the area
header simply lists a different cast, and throw_enable decides
whether they can throw.  Nothing is chosen at run time.

Note $52A4 ORs sactor_def3/4/5 together and only proceeds when all
are zero -- the area's item appears once those slots are clear.  It
tests the slots, not kills, which is why an enemy that wanders off
screen releases the item just as a killed one does.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:65EA:
----------------------------------------------------------------
RelocateSpecialActor -- puts special actor X back on screen at a
RANDOM position rather than wrapping it around.

    sactor_pos_long  = random & $3F + $48     ->  $48-$87
    sactor_pos_cross = random & $3F + $44     ->  $44-$83

Then FindValidPlacement checks the spot with $D01B and, if it is not
placeable, nudges both axes by a random amount in -$10..+$0F and
tries again.  place_retries ($C3) allows four attempts, or none at
all when $1E73 is non-zero; running out returns with carry clear.

This is why an enemy that leaves the screen, or is carried off by the
view scrolling, reappears somewhere unrelated -- often on the
opposite side.  It is not wrap-around; the actor is simply dropped at
a fresh random walkable spot inside a fixed band.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6657:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ProjectileVsSpecialActors -- the three projectile slots against the
four special actors.  This is the damage model the tough enemies
use, and it is NOT the $A0 one.

Overlap test: +/-$08 on the long axis, a variable box on the cross
axis taken from $40/$41.  On a hit:

    sfx $10, sactor_flash ($1E99,X) = $0A
    JSR sub_4F6C                    despawn the projectile
    if weapon_level != 0: JSR $D030
    LDA sactor_damage ($1E81,X)
    CLC
    ADC weapon_level
    BCC still_alive                 no carry -> store and continue
      JSR $D030
      sactor_damage = $0C           carry out of bit 7 -> DEAD
  still_alive:
    sactor_damage = A

So damage ACCUMULATES in sactor_damage and death is an 8-bit
overflow -- reaching $100 -- rather than crossing $A0.  An actor
seeded with S needs 256-S points, so these are far tougher than
anything in the eight-slot array: with the blaster at +2 a value
around $80 costs roughly 64 hits.

weapon_level is added here exactly as it is for ordinary actors, so
the knife (level 0) adds nothing and can never kill a special actor
either, however long it is used.

$529E ORs sactor_damage across all four slots and only releases the
area's item when every one is zero.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f7:F280:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ExpandAreaDef -- unpacks one area-header byte into a pair.

    high nibble -> A, via tbl_DefAmount
        $00 $01 $02 $04 $08 $0C $10 $14 $1E $28 $32 $3C $46 $7F $FF
    low nibble  -> X, via tbl_DefRateMask
        $FF $7F $3F $1F $0F $07 $03 $01 $01 $01 ...

The caller stores A and X into consecutive slots, so each of the six
per-area definitions at $1E6A-$1E75 is an (amount, rate mask) pair
packed into a single header byte.

The mask table is the classic descending AND-mask ladder used to gate
periodic behaviour -- the same shape as the throw rate mask at $8D --
so the low nibble sets how often something happens and the high
nibble how much or how many.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6436:
----------------------------------------------------------------
tbl_SactorToughness -- the seed written into sactor_damage when a
special actor is created, indexed by sactor_kind ($1E91,X).

Because death is an 8-bit overflow of sactor_damage, an entry S
costs 256-S points, and each hit adds weapon_level:

  kind  seed  points   axe(+1)  blaster(+2)  mega(+3)
    0   $FC      4        4         2           2
    1   $FE      2        2         1           1
    2   $F9      7        7         4           3
    3   $F4     12       12         6           4
    4   $F8      8        8         4           3
    5   $F7      9        9         5           3
    6   $F1     15       15         8           5
    8   $C4     60       60        30          20
    9   $C4     60       60        30          20
   12   $EC     20       20        10           7
   13   $B0     80       80        40          27
   14   $B0     80       80        40          27
   15   $B4     76       76        38          26

The knife is weapon_level 0 and adds nothing, so it cannot kill any
of these however long it is used.

sactor_kind ($1E91,X) is the enemy-kind field: PickSactorKind
($6741) returns it, it is stored alongside the actor, and it selects
this seed.  Creation also decrements sactor_def4 ($1E72), so the
area's definition slots act as a remaining-population count.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.b5:B4D7:
Hit test: long against boss_pos+box_lo..box_hi, cross against
box_cross_lo..hi. For Dr. Evil the long box is the moving ear.
headers.f7:D40B:
----------------------------------------------------------------
DamageHealth -- reached through the bank 7 vector $D036.  A holds
the amount of health to remove.

    PHA
    LDA itm_cross ($1F3E)
    BEQ full
      PLA : LSR A : PHA      <-- carrying the CROSS halves the damage
  full:
    PLA : EOR #$FF : SEC : ADC hp_cur     ; hp_cur - amount
    CMP #$DC : BCC store                  ; underflow guard
    LDA #$00                              ; clamp at zero
  store:
    STA hp_cur

So the cross is the game's damage-reduction item and it applies to
EVERY health source, not just one kind of enemy.  Combined with its
two effects in the contact handler at $5FA7 -- selected, it blocks
blood loss outright; merely owned, it halves it -- the cross does
three separate jobs:

    selected : immune to contact blood loss
    owned    : contact blood loss halved
    owned    : ALL health damage halved

Note the underflow guard uses $DC rather than a simple carry test,
so a hit larger than current health clamps to zero rather than
wrapping.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5D22:
----------------------------------------------------------------
SetActorVelocity -- the whole of the ordinary enemy AI.

Two steps.  First, home in on the target coordinates in $40/$41:

    vel_long  = (pos_long  < target) ? +1 : -1
    vel_cross = (pos_cross < target) ? +1 : -1

That alone would make every enemy walk straight at the player.  The
second step randomises it by masking one axis away:

    Y = Random & 3
    vel_cross &= dat_5D52[Y]     ; $FF $FF $FF $00
    vel_long  &= dat_5D56[Y]     ; $FF $FF $00 $FF

So per update:
    Y=0,1   both axes kept   -> diagonal, straight at the player
    Y=2     long axis zeroed -> moves only across
    Y=3     cross axis zeroed-> moves only along

Half the time it charges diagonally, a quarter it slides one way, a
quarter the other.  The direction is never away from the player, so
an enemy always converges -- the randomness only chooses how
directly.  That is what produces the shambling-but-inevitable
approach, with no state machine and no pathfinding: eight bytes of
table and one random number.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:6744:
----------------------------------------------------------------
PickSactorKind -- decides which kind of special actor a screen gets.

    LDY screen_kind_idx ($8A)
    LDA tbl_ScreenKind,Y
    BPL done                  ; positive -> that IS the kind, fixed
    AND #$07                  ; negative -> low 3 bits are a mask
    JSR Random
    AND mask                  ; kind = Random & mask
  done:

So each screen either pins one enemy kind or draws randomly from a
range.  The 80-entry table holds fixed kinds ($01, $06, $07, $08,
$09, $0A, $0C) and random specs ($F3 -> kinds 0-3, $F7 and $FF ->
kinds 0-7).

This is where regional enemy variety comes from: the area header
says how many and how often, this table says which kind, and
tbl_SactorToughness turns the kind into hit points.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f7:D304:
----------------------------------------------------------------
AddScore -- reached through the bank 7 vector $D030.  A holds the
points to award.

The score is seven UNPACKED DECIMAL DIGITS at score_digits ($27E8),
one digit per byte, most significant first.  The routine adds A to
the lowest digit and propagates carries by repeated subtraction:

    LDX #$06
  digit:
    ADC score_digits,X
    while result >= 10: subtract 10 and INC the digit above
    store, carry 0 into the next digit, DEX

Callers pass small constants -- $02, $08, $0A, $14, $32, $50 -- at
kills and pickups.

Note the address: the terrain grid occupies $2400-$27E7, so the
score sits immediately above it.  That is an independent confirmation
of the grid's extent derived from MapTileAt's strip table.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:4B6D:
----------------------------------------------------------------
ScreenIndexToWorldPos -- how rooms connect.

There is no exit table and no adjacency graph, because screens are
not nodes.  screen_idx ($56) with world_pos_hi ($57) is a 16-BIT
WORLD POSITION along the long axis, and a screen number is just an
arithmetic slice of it:

    positive index:  pos = (index * 8) + $20      ($4B99)
    negative index:  pos = map_limit - offset     ($4B87)
                     offset $01 normally, $4A when the index is $FE

The wrap case is the map's far edge: walking off one end sets the
position to map_limit minus a small offset, putting the player at
the opposite extreme.

And at $53C3 the relationship runs the other way -- screen_idx is
overwritten straight from the player's own coordinates:

    screen_idx    = player_x_lo
    world_pos_hi  = player_x_hi

So "which room am I in" is not stored or looked up; it is read off
the player's position every step.  Adjacency is implicit in the
coordinate system, which is why no link table exists to be found.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:579B:
Terrain_HurtingGround -- terrain $A1, the counterpart to the well.
Calls DamageHealth with 2, sets terrain_timer to $0A so it can only
bite once every ten frames, and plays sound $11.  Confirmed in play
as damaging ground; it appears in the mansion basement.

    $A0  well of health   +1 hp per tick, clamped to hp_max
    $A1  hurting ground   -2 hp per tick, halved to -1 by the cross
headers.b5:B683:
----------------------------------------------------------------
tbl_BossBit -- FOUR entries, indexed by mode_flag, not eight.  Only
three progression bits exist, one per boss:

    mode_flag $00  ->  $00   not a boss fight
    mode_flag $01  ->  $02   skull boss    -> bit 1
    mode_flag $02  ->  $01   ram boss      -> bit 0
    mode_flag $03  ->  $04   Dr. Evil      -> bit 2

Every test of boss_flags in the ROM masks with $01, $02 or $04 and
nothing else, so bits 3-7 are unused.  The bytes following this table
are not masks; an earlier reading of it as eight entries was reading
past the end.

What each bit unlocks:
    bit 0 (ram)      terrain $85 and $86 -- the mansion squares that
                     otherwise refuse and draw glyph $38/$39
    bit 1 (skull)    tested at f6:$5815 and b0:$A44D
    bit 2 (Dr Evil)  f7:$F231 -- with the pumpkin not yet held, sets
                     item_type $05 so the plasmic pumpkin appears.
                     That is the drop on Dr. Evil's death.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5813:
----------------------------------------------------------------
BossDoorGate -- terrain codes $F0 and above: the boss arena doors.

The gate is a LOCK-OUT, not a lock-in.  $89 holds the pending screen
kind (read at $4B63 into screen_kind_idx), so storing to it is what
performs the transition; the bare RTS at $5839 does nothing.

    $F1   bit 1 (skull)    SET -> RTS, door dead
                         CLEAR -> transition
    $F2   bit 0 (ram)      SET -> RTS, door dead
                         CLEAR -> transition
    else  bit 2 (Dr Evil)  SET -> RTS, door dead
                         CLEAR -> transition

So each boss door works until that boss is beaten, then stops
responding.  It prevents re-entering an arena you have already
cleared, rather than requiring the kill to get in.

Confirmed from play: the $F2 square on the layout shared by the
screens using property table $DB00 is the door to the ram boss.
----------------------------------------------------------------
headers.f6:5166:
DrawItemIcon -- skips when item_type is zero or has bit 7 set.
Bit 7 marks the item as PENDING: it exists, with its authored
position from the area header, but is not yet drawn or collectable.
$51B5 routes a pending item to the release check at $529C, and
$52B0 clears the bit with AND #$7F once the condition passes.

So $8E is a pending blaster, $82 a pending crypt key, $88 a pending
diamond.  There is no separate class of high-bit item -- it is the
same item waiting to appear.
headers.f6:4006: MusicPlay(A = song number) -- trampoline callable from any bank.
headers.f6:752F:
Note-on for voice X. Note byte 0 = instrument<<4 | duration index,
byte 1 = AUDF pitch (0 = rest).
headers.f6:757B:
Per-voice envelope step -- dispatches through JMP (music_env_vec)
to one of five handlers. Indirect, so these are declared entries.
headers.f6:7F68:
Song table: 4 bytes per song = voice 0 track pointer, voice 1 track
pointer. Pointers into $8000-$BFFF are resolved against whatever bank
is mapped when the song is started, so each bank carries its own music.
headers.b5:B013:
BossSetup(A = boss 1-3): read a 32-byte record via tbl_BossSetupLo.
Fields +6..+9 are skipped when $1F9D is set -- the re-entry path.
headers.b5:B28B:
Per-frame boss update. Three-way dispatch on mode_flag; each boss
is its own hand-written routine, not a shared engine.
headers.b5:B9EF:
BossFire(A = mask). Fires only when Random AND mask == 0, so the
mask is the reciprocal of the rate. It shrinks as boss_stage climbs.
headers.b5:B3C0:
Fire-rate mask by boss_stage: 1-in-64 at the start, $00 (every
frame) by stage 13. Index +5 while boss_flash is set.
headers.b5:B3D4:
Dr. Evil. Bit 7 of $45 selects one of two hitboxes on the long axis
($2E-$38 or $66-$70), swapping about every 4.3 seconds. Only the
current side can be hit, and $5B records which -- the fire routine
reads it back so the shot leaves the ear that is currently weak.
headers.b5:BAEB:
Spawn point follows the weak spot: $5B == 0 -> boss_pos+$34,
otherwise boss_pos+$66.
headers.b5:BB90:
Walk all eight actor slots and test each against the player. This is
what makes Dr. Evil's crawling bug (slot 7) hurt on contact like a shot.
headers.b5:BAA9:
Dr. Evil's crawling bug: slot 7, vel_cross = 0 so it travels dead
level, vel_long +/-1 so it crawls. Enters at the player's cross
position; side comes from boss_stage & 1. Takes priority over the
ear shot -- spawning one skips the shot that frame.

notes.f6:
Main game engine.  Permanently mapped, holds the vector table, the
DLI handlers, the main loop and most game logic.
notes.f7:
Fixed high bank.  $C000-$CFFF is graphics data, $D000-$FFFF is code
(support routines, the per-area descriptor tables and RESET).
notes.b0:
$8000-$9FFF is empty ($00 fill).  Code lives at $A000-$A6xx behind a
small JMP table at $A000; $A2xx is the text renderer.  From ~$A6A3 to the
end of the bank is the game's dialogue/story script (see TEXT.md).
notes.b3: Code at $8000 (entered via JSR $8000 after selecting bank 3).
notes.b5: Data plus a code block entered at $B000.
notes.b7: Bank 7 seen through the $8000 window (rarely, if ever, used).
